outOfOffice.autoReply: On leave until Sep 2. For portfolio escalations contact Sara Lindqvist. For anything board-facing contact Yuki Tanaka.

messages.body: Week 1. I chaired SteerCo today. Three things you will want to know. (1) SPARK M2 was called NO-GO on Aug 11 — Daniel had 88% and the remaining integration testing against ATLAS multi-tenant was not going to close in a day. New target Aug 25. Nobody argued; the honest call was the right one. (2) SHIELD readiness criteria — Fatima tabled a definition yesterday, five acceptance items and James Whitfield as the named signer. I-004 is on a path. (3) Apple has not answered on HORIZON. Priya is drafting the Android-only contingency rather than waiting. I told her to write it as a decision, not a fallback. Nothing needs you this week.

Week 2, and this is the week it turned. Apple REJECTED on Aug 19 — guideline 5.1.1(v), no in-app account deletion path. Fix was three days of work, resubmitted Aug 24. Second review clock starts from scratch. Ingrid and Priya held a contingency call Aug 20 (you were invited) and decided to ship Android-only on Aug 31 and hold iOS for the resubmission. I think that is the right call and I said so, but I want to flag clearly: it was taken in a call, there is no decision record, and it changes what M8 means. That is yours to ratify. Good news to balance it — MERIDIAN M6 closed Aug 20 at 210/210, a day early against the DR-015 revised date. The two engineers worked. James has told Kai Muller the v1 EoL date holds at Sep 30.

Week 3. Two problems and one you need to plan around. (1) PULSE traffic verification found 14 pipelines still writing to Airflow-managed state — precisely the A-006 blind spot, found by doing the thing rather than by planning it. Yuna has moved read-only mode from Sep 1 to Sep 14. She is not yet saying Sep 30 is gone, but I would not bet on it, and it is $380K a month. (2) The Q3 QBR moved. Marcus Bauer's office pulled it from Sep 22 to Sep 8 on Aug 24 to land before the board pack cut-off. Pre-read is due Sep 4 EOD, which is the day after you are back. I have not written it. I did not think it was mine to write. (3) SPARK M2 closed Aug 27, sixteen days late. Daniel and Leo have already agreed M3 moves to Oct 16. Also no decision record. Also yours.

Last note before you are back. SHIELD readiness signed off Aug 31 by James Whitfield against Fatima's five criteria — that one landed clean. Observation window opened Sep 1. But DEP-009 did not close: the two PULSE-dependent controls (CC6.4, CC6.6) went into the window on the July compensating documentation, not on the Temporal audit trail, because Yuna was underwater on the decommission. Fatima raised it yesterday and is waiting on someone senior to say whether that is acceptable for ninety days or whether we re-evidence inside the window. I did not want to make that call for you. Everything else is in the threads. Welcome back — the QBR pre-read is the thing I would open first.

threads.subject: Q3 QBR moved to Sep 8 — pre-read due Sep 4 EOD

messages.body: Karl — moving the Q3 QBR from Sep 22 to Sep 8, 14:00, to land inside the board pack cut-off. Pre-read due Sep 4 EOD. Three things I need in writing and will not accept verbally on the day: (1) the PULSE dual-run reconciliation — accrued to date, monthly burn, and the date the burn actually stops, which I understand is not the same as the date the pipelines moved; (2) ATLAS M9, 15 enterprise customers by Dec 31 — I have seen 3 in production since July and I want the renegotiated number, not a recovery plan; (3) SPARK's Dec 31 GA chain end to end, since M2 has now moved twice. I know you are out. I am sending this so it is waiting for you.

Noted. Karl, do not try to answer this from a beach. Sep 4 is fine but let us talk before you send anything on ATLAS M9 — I want us aligned on the number before Marcus sees it. I have put 30 minutes in your Friday morning.

threads.subject: App Store rejection — 5.1.1(v) account deletion. Resubmitted Aug 24.

messages.body: Apple rejected today, day 18 of review. Guideline 5.1.1(v) — an app offering account creation must offer in-app account deletion. We route deletion through the web console. This is a known, well-documented requirement and we should have caught it in pre-submission review; I own that. Engineering estimate is three days. A-002 in the RAID log assumed a 2–3 week review and a first-pass approval. Half of that assumption was right.

Resubmitted this morning with in-app deletion. The review clock restarts — expect a decision Sep 7–14 on the same 2–3 week window, and I am no longer treating that window as reliable. Aug 31 public GA on iOS is gone. Android ships Aug 31 per the Aug 20 call.

Status for your return: Android public GA shipped Aug 31 on time, 4,100 installs in the first 48 hours, no SEV incidents. iOS is on day 10 of the second review. Two things I need from you and cannot resolve at my level: Jennifer Wu wants a written iOS date for Solaris by Sep 4 and I do not have one to give; and I-005 is still open — mobile post-GA support has no run owner, and public GA has roughly tripled L1 mobile volume since Aug 31. The DR-012 engineer is now doing run work that nobody scoped.

Summarising the call: we ship Android publicly on Aug 31 and hold iOS for the resubmission rather than delaying both. Reasoning — Solaris and Kestrel are both majority-Android estates, a staged launch we chose reads better than a launch we missed, and holding Android to keep the platforms paired buys nothing. Marketing runs the Aug 31 campaign as an Android launch with iOS 'weeks away'. Karl, you were on the invite; I did not want to hold the decision three weeks for you. If you disagree when you are back, say so and we will re-cut the messaging, but the ship has left on the Android side.

threads.subject: Solaris Logistics — need a written iOS date before Sep 4

messages.body: Solaris signature is scheduled Sep 15, $2.4M, and their procurement lead has now asked me twice for an iOS availability date in writing. This is their third date conversation with us this year and I have run out of ways to say 'soon'. I need something defensible, even if it is a range with a stated dependency.

Escalating: their legal review starts Sep 4 and they want the mobile availability language settled before it opens. If I have nothing by Sep 4 they will either strike the iOS clause — which cuts scope and price — or push signature past Sep 15. I would rather give them a conservative date we can hold than another 'imminent'.

threads.subject: Observation window opened Sep 1 — CC6.4 / CC6.6 went in on the old evidence

messages.body: Readiness signed off today. James signed against the five criteria agreed Aug 13: 100/100 controls with accepted evidence, named owner per control, monitoring live on all 100, drift detection armed, and a documented exception path. Deloitte confirmed the observation window opens Sep 1 and closes Nov 30, report Dec 15. That is M6 closed on the board-mandated date, and the definition of 'ready' now exists in writing, which it did not three weeks ago.

One thing did not land and I need a portfolio-level call on it. DEP-009 — re-evidencing CC6.4 and CC6.6 against the completed Temporal audit trail — did not happen before Sep 1. Yuna was consumed by the decommission and I did not escalate hard enough. Those two controls entered the observation window on the July compensating documentation, which Deloitte accepted for readiness but which is the weakest evidence in the pack. Two options. (a) Leave them and re-evidence at the first quarterly cycle, accepting that if Deloitte samples them early we are defending compensating docs for a control that has a real audit trail sitting unused. (b) Re-evidence inside the window in September, which is clean but means changing evidence mid-observation and telling Deloitte why. I have a mild preference for (b) done early and disclosed, but this is exactly the $12.2M question and I do not want to choose alone. R-009 is no longer theoretical — it has a specific name on day one.

threads.subject: PULSE decommission — 14 pipelines still writing Airflow state, read-only slips to Sep 14

messages.body: Traffic verification result, week 3 of 7. 14 pipelines are running on Temporal but still writing state into Airflow-managed metadata tables. They pass every functional check and they would have failed silently at shutdown. This is A-006 exactly: the sequence was never rehearsed on this estate, and the runbook did not know what actually depended on what. Same defect class as INC-2026-0126. Read-only mode moves from Sep 1 to Sep 14.

Separately — INC-2026-0131, SEV2 Aug 26. A traffic-verification cutover dropped a DataCore ingestion pipeline for 4h11m. Detected in 9 minutes, no customer-visible data loss, backfill completed same day. Post-incident review Sep 4. It is a self-inflicted wound from the decommission work, and it is the argument for not compressing the remaining sequence.

Where this leaves Sep 30: read-only Sep 14, then a minimum two-week soak before shutdown puts us at Sep 28 with zero margin, and that assumes the remaining verification finds nothing else. I am not asking to move the date yet. I am telling you that I will know by Sep 14 and that every week past Sep 30 is $380K. Dual-run accrued is $2.13M as of Sep 1.

threads.subject: SPARK M2 closed Aug 27 — proposing M3 to Oct 16

messages.body: Calling NO-GO on M2 today. 88% with the remaining 12% being integration testing against ATLAS multi-tenant serving, and ATLAS engineers are only now coming off the uptime work. Forcing a close today would mean declaring an alpha that has not been integration tested, which is the kind of green that turns red in September. New target Aug 25.

M2 closed today, Aug 27 — 16 days late against Aug 11, 2 days late against the revised Aug 25. Model serving alpha is live and integration tested against ATLAS multi-tenant. DEP-008 closed. Leo and I have agreed M3 (visual workflow builder beta) moves from Sep 30 to Oct 16: M3 could not start until the M2 architecture patterns existed, that was Aug 31 not Aug 25, and the team needs six clear weeks. Consequence we are not pretending about: the Dec 31 GA chain now has M3 Oct 16 → M5 Nov 30 → GA Dec 31, which removes the last of the slack and makes M5 the next pressure point. VantagePoint's Sep 15 roadmap review is fine — M2 is closed and demonstrable. M6 evaluation framework missed Aug 31 at 52%; it competed with M2 for the same engineers all month and lost. No new date on M6 yet.

threads.subject: NEXUS M7 target — is it <200 or <175? Board chart is being built

messages.body: Raising this in its own thread so it does not get lost in the cover notes, because it has been open since Jul 13 and it now has a deadline. The KR says fewer than 200 services. CHG-002 says fewer than 175. Redmount's letter cited service count specifically. The Q3 board trajectory chart is being built for the Sep 8 QBR pack and whoever builds it has to pick one. We are at 223 today, down from 247 on Aug 10, holding roughly 6 a week — which hits <200 comfortably by Dec 31 and does not hit <175. That difference is the entire story the chart tells. Please pick before Sep 4.

threads.subject: ATLAS — 4th enterprise customer live, and M9 needs a QBR slot

messages.body: 4th enterprise customer onboarded today — Halden Freight, live and stable. 4/5 on M7 with Sep 15 comfortable; the 5th is in contracting with Dmitri. Uptime has held between 98.9% and 99.2% every day since the rate limit lifted Aug 3. F7 autoscaling is at 80% and tracking to Sep 15. August month average will land at 99.1%, first month above the 99.0% commitment since GA.

M9 is the one I cannot fix by executing harder. 4 in production, 15 by Dec 31, four months left. That needs 2.75 a month against a demonstrated pace of roughly one. The honest renegotiated number is 8, maybe 9 if the pipeline converts. This has been an open decision since Aug 3 and Marcus Bauer is now asking for it directly. It needs to be settled in the QBR pre-read, not in the QBR.

M6 closed today at 210/210, one day ahead of the DR-015 revised date. The two dedicated engineers cleared all 8 bespoke integrations in 17 days. Per-customer status to Ingrid weekly, as she asked. Kai Muller has the confirmed Sep 30 v1 EoL date and Thornbridge's $1.7M expansion moved to Contract Negotiation on Aug 24.

One caveat I want on the record rather than buried. Two of the eight — Brightline Logistics and Corvid Systems — are on v2 via a compatibility shim that translates their legacy webhook signatures. The shim runs on v1 infrastructure. It has to be removed and replaced with native integrations before the Sep 30 shutdown or those two customers break at EoL. Four weeks of work, currently owned by nobody, and it is not visible in the 210/210 number. SMB reached 96% Aug 25.
